To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the optimal spam and email virus detection system is not the one that maximizes the probability of detection, (2) there is an optimal level of security that minimizes the total expected costs, and (3) the total costs of spam and email virus is a convex function of the security level.
the cost of a security breach is much higher than what is commonly perceived.

the university can save $1.2 million per annum by investing in an email and spam security system that has a 99 percent probability of detecting spam and virus emails and has a 99.5 percent probability of not detecting non-spam emails.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of determining optimal detection and prevention strategy in a corporate setting.
the problem of justifiability of security investments and how to justify the investments in the context of spam and email virus problem.
the following: (i) the optimal configuration of a detection system for spam and email virus, and (ii) the justification of the security investment for spam and email viruses.

a mid-size university should invest in spam and e-mail virus security systems.
the university should invest in the spam and virus security system and the optimal configuration is a combination of anti-spam, anti-virus, and firewall technologies.
the university should invest in a security system with a 95% detection rate for spam and virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it demonstrates the use of ROC curves to justify security investments in spam and e-mail virus detection systems.
the decision to invest in a spam email and virus security system is not an easy one.
a university should invest in an anti-spam and anti-virus system with a detection rate of 90% and a false alarm rate of 1%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal configuration of a detection system is a function of not only technology specific detection costs, but also of other costs.
the cost of a false positive can be as important as the cost of a true positive.
